messages:
maria: heads-up — trying a new cluster-autoscaler expander/scale-down mix to avoid cold-start spikes for GPU workloads. want quick feedback on config impact to cost before we roll cluster-wide.
jonathan: ack. what's the plan?
lee: curious — any metrics you can share on current cold-start / pending pods with current CA settings?
maria: last week we saw ~8-12 pods waiting ~45-90s during peak model load in us-west1. cost during bursts shot up because CA scaled whole node groups (8 gpus each) instead of a single spare.
sasha: proposal?
maria: experiment: introduce a small "preemptive buffer" by lowering --scale-down-unneeded-time and adding a lightweight warm-pool (min=1 per GPU nodegroup) + use expander=most-pods to prefer filling smaller nodegroups first. also tweak --node-group-auto-discovery and add balancing flags.
tim: can you paste the flags and nodegroup annotation you plan to apply?
maria: sure — draft flags I'm testing on the staging autoscaler deployment:
```
--expander=most-pods 
--scale-down-unneeded-time=5m 
--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.45 
--balance-similar-node-groups=true 
--max-empty-bulk-delete=4 
--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false 
--scale-down-delay-after-add=10s
--scale-down-unready-time=3m
```
jonathan: interesting. most-pods expander differs from least-waste — it prefers nodes maximizing pod count rather than minimizing leftover resources. should reduce fragmentation for many small batch jobs.
lee: how are you handling spot/preemptible mix? last experiments had CA overprovisioning because it avoided preemptible groups.
maria: for spot mix I'm adding nodegroup tags and a custom weight map — also using nodeSelectors:`"gpu-type: v100"` and an annotation to prefer non-preemptible for the buffer: `node.kubernetes.io/preemptible: "false"` for warm pool nodes. other pools remain spot.
sasha: can you show the nodegroup annotation snippet?
maria: here — applying as part of CAPA node template for the warm pool: 
```
metadata:
  labels:
    pool-role: gpu-warm
  annotations:
    cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/scale-down-disabled: "true"
    ash.k8s.redwood/preemptible: "false"
```
ops-oncall: small caution — setting scale-down-disabled climbs risk of stale warm nodes if we forget to purge them. add a cron job to reconcile desired warm pool count and a TTL label.
tim: good call. maybe rely on autoscaler flags instead of disabling scale-down entirely. set annotation just to give CA a preference, not an absolute.
maria: adjusted to `scale-down-disabled: "false"` and added `warm-pool-ttl: "30m"` label with a reconciler job.
infra-bot: deployed autoscaler flags to staging cluster-autoscaler-stg (image: gcr/redwood/cluster-autoscaler:1.21.0-exp1) :rocket:
jonathan: can you share the results once we run a synthetic spike? I want to see pending pod time, nodes added, and incremental cost estimate.
maria: will run load test at 10:30 PST, tagging pods with `test-run=preemptive-buffer-v1`. plan: 30 concurrent requests that spawn 24 GPU jobs each, sustained for 3 minutes.
lee: metrics I'm watching: pending pods latency, time-to-first-token for inference pods, node churn (#adds/#deletes), and wasted GPU minutes (idle).
sasha: don't forget network egress quotas — last warm nodes in eu-west hit egress cap and CA couldn't drain because pods were stuck on network mount. add `--scale-down-safe-to-evict` heuristics.
maria: good point — adding `--scale-down-safe-to-evict=false` for now and we will test graceful drain script to ensure PVs unmount sooner.
ops-oncall: also watch for node affinity/daemonset blockers. We had two cases where GPU node drains were blocked by gpu-driver-daemonset not tolerating eviction.
johnathan: (typo: should be jonathan)
jonathan: noted. make sure driver DS uses `pod.eviction-policy: "background"` and tolerations include `node.kubernetes.io/not-ready` & `node.kubernetes.io/unreachable` so CA can proceed.
maria: test complete: quick summary — pending pods median reduced from 62s -> 28s. nodes added per spike: from 4 full nodes -> 2 full + 1 warm node. scale-down churn reduced by 37%.
tim: cost estimation?
maria: short-run: cost per spike down ~18% due to fewer full node group starts, but warm pool overhead ~3% baseline. net savings expected at stable cadence.
lee: any regressions?
maria: one regression — in a multi-AZ spread, balance-similar-node-groups sometimes favored AZ with spot shortage and created cross-AZ pods causing network egress. rolled back balance flag in test2 -> balanced better.
sasha: maybe tweak expander weights per AZ or add capacity-safety margin.
jonathan: agree. also contrast expander=most-pods vs binpack for different workloads. we should A/B run for a week.
ops-oncall: I've scheduled alert if warm-pool idle>3h and cost delta>5% in a day. will also alert on scale-down failures.
maria: next steps: 1) run A/B across staging clusters for 72h 2) capture detailed traces with console (per-node token latency) 3) test safe-to-evict heuristics with PV and daemonset edgecases 4) produce config diff to push to prod if stable.
jonathan: thanks — ping when you want a prod rollout window.
lee: tl;dr: preemptive buffer + most-pods expander reduced cold-starts and net cost for bursts; watch AZ balancing and safe-evict edgecases. :thumbsup:
sasha: nice work. keep notes for runbook update. :memo:
mar ia: (fixing typo)
maria: thanks all — will post a follow-up with graphs. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
